item.title: C/River imposes curfew on Iso-Bendeghe, Boje over deadly land clashes
item.description: .bans entry into disputed areas, orders security agencies to enforce order By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Government has imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Iso-Bendeghe and Boje communities in Boki Local Government Area, following protracted clashes over a land dispute between the two neighbours. The curfew, announced Wednesday in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Pst. Ekpenyong Cobham, will last one week from November 24, 2026. Cobham said the measure became necessary because the crisis was threatening the peace of the area. “This has become necessary as the situation has continued to threaten lives, property and peace in the area,” he said. Under the order, no movement is allowed in either community from 6 pm to 6 am daily. The statement also barred residents of both communities from entering or moving into the disputed areas “for any reason.” Security agencies were directed to enforce the curfew strictly. The government warned that violators would face the full weight of the law. “Defaulters will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the Commissioner said. The state government appealed to community leaders, youths and other stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign. It said it remained committed to ending the hostilities between the two communities. “This administration remains committed to restoring lasting peace between the two communities and appeals to leaders, youths and all stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign,” the statement said. Cobham added that the government would keep a close watch on developments in the area. “The government will continue to monitor the situation closely until normalcy returns in the area,” he said. item.title: CAF releases finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award (Full list)
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has released the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, Senegal’s Sadio Mané and three other players making the shortlist. The final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for club and country during the period under consideration. Morocco has three representatives on the list, while Senegal has two, reflecting the countries’ strong performances in the period. Hakimi, who plays for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after helping the club win the UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 title. The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON. The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph. Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals. Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI. Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals. The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos. The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition. item.title: Meta unveils $700,000 AI grant for Nigerian startups
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Meta has announced a $700,000 artificial intelligence (AI) grant programme for startups and developers in Nigeria and six other countries, as part of efforts to accelerate AI innovation and expand access to emerging technologies. The programme, scheduled to commence in 2027, will cover Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to a statement issued by the company on Tuesday. Meta said the grant would support startups and developers building solutions using its AI tools and wearable technologies. The company also announced the launch of a new hub designed to provide educational resources and information on its AI developments, partnerships and innovation initiatives across Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. The hub will operate through three learning programmes: AI Academy, AI Literacy and AI for Small and Medium-sized Businesses. The programmes are designed for students, developers, entrepreneurs and business professionals, with Meta targeting more than five million beneficiaries across the three regions over the next three years. Meta’s Vice-President of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Turkey, Kojo Boakye, said the initiatives were designed to equip developers and entrepreneurs with the skills, resources and support needed to build AI solutions that address challenges in their communities. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives,” Boakye said. “Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. “The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built.” In another initiative, Meta announced the AMET AI Awards 2026, with more than $100,000 in prizes across seven categories to recognise outstanding AI innovations. The company said the awards would recognise finalists from its AI Academy and Wearables Studio programmes, including students, developers and startups. The award categories include Wearables Innovation of the Year, AI Builder of the Year, Emerging Innovator of the Year and Startup of the Year. Others are AI for Accessibility and Inclusion, AI for Social and Economic Impact, and People’s Choice, which will be decided through a live vote by attendees at the summit. Meta said the awards would recognise projects leveraging AI-powered technologies to address everyday needs, improve access to opportunities and services, and promote social and economic development. item.title: Zamfara: Bandits kill two headmasters, 13 others, abduct residents
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Armed bandits have killed 15 people, including two primary school headmasters and an 11-month-old baby, in separate attacks on communities in Zamfara State. The attacks, which occurred in Tungan Janbuzu and Madanbaji communities, also left several residents abducted, according to a report by the BBC Hausa Service. The two headmasters, identified as Kabiru Salisu and Shehu Umar, both aged 35, were reportedly killed in an ambush at Janbuzu. A resident of the community, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 4pm, following the escape of some kidnapped residents from their captors. He explained that the bandits had earlier abducted some locals from Janbuzu and kept them in captivity, forcing them to work for their captors. According to him, the kidnappers had demanded a ransom of N300,000, which was subsequently delivered to them at a location near Kiawa. He said the bandits collected the money but later drove the person who delivered it away, claiming that the payment was meant for recharge cards and fuel. The resident further narrated that the bandits had taken six captives into the bush, tied them up and left them under the supervision of a young boy while they went to Aboro to purchase drugs and other supplies. However, the captives reportedly managed to untie themselves, overpower their guard, seize his gun and escape after beating him. The resident said the escape angered other members of the gang, who were reportedly hiding on a nearby farm. He said the armed men subsequently ambushed the two headmasters near a location known as Gora, seized their mobile phones and shot them dead. The resident, however, said kidnapping incidents had reduced considerably in the area, except in communities located close to the forests and bushes where the bandits operate. He expressed concern over the continued vulnerability of residents in remote settlements, despite the reported reduction in kidnapping incidents. item.title: When did Nigerian law prescribe death for election rigging? — APC’s Morka asks Obi, NDC
item.description: By Bayo Wahab The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has questioned the legal basis for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC)’s “rig and die” slogan, asking when Nigerian law prescribed the death penalty for electoral offences. Morka said anyone accused of rigging an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law, rather than subjected to punishment determined by political parties or their supporters. The APC spokesman spoke on News Central on Wednesday while reacting to allegations of violence by NDC supporters against members of the ruling party. His comments followed remarks by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after the party’s town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday. Obi had dismissed concerns over the message, insisting that the supporters were opposed to election rigging, not political campaigns. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said. However, reacting to the explanation, Morka said the slogan was inflammatory and questioned the implication of allowing individuals to determine who had rigged an election and should therefore die. “Now, what does that mean? What message are you sending when you appoint yourself as custodians of elections, and therefore anyone you consider to have rigged an election — because that’s a subjective standard — should die,” he said. Morka said he had watched a video in which Obi defended the statement, adding that the NDC candidate had acknowledged that the message was “rig and die” rather than “campaign and die”. The APC spokesman then challenged Obi and the NDC to explain the legal justification for such a position. “So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked. Morka maintained that anyone suspected of electoral malpractice should be apprehended and made to face the consequences provided by law. “I think as a lawyer and as a citizen, that anyone who rigs an election should be apprehended and be made to face the law as provided by the law, not as provided by Peter Obi or the NDC stalwarts who make this very incendiary comment,” he said. Beyond the slogan, Morka also accused the NDC of making unsubstantiated allegations of violence against the APC without formally reporting the incidents to the police or seeking investigations by independent authorities. “So when the NDC comes out and they make allegations, if you look at all the allegations they make, there’s not one that they have managed or even attempted to furnish any kind of substantiation,” he said. item.title: CBN raises BDC’s dollar cash limit to $1m weekly
item.description: …Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. item.title: ‘Ebube Dike’: Tinubu pays tribute to late Nollywood legend Pete Edochie
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab President Bola Tinubu has mourned veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, describing his death as a great loss to Nigeria and the film industry. Tinubu said Edochie was one of the progenitors of Nigeria’s vibrant film industry and an exceptional actor whose contributions to African storytelling would remain memorable for generations. The President, while stating this in a tribute shared on the official X account of his Special Adviser Information and Strategy, recalled the late actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart , in the 1980s. Describing the actor as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians, Tinubu said, “Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor – one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on the screen and in person. “He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter, and charm to many homes.” The President also recalled Edochie’s performances in productions such as Igodo , Rituals and Lionheart , noting that they helped shape the evolution and international visibility of Nollywood. According to him, the actor’s portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values and human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide. Tinubu further highlighted Edochie’s contributions beyond acting, describing him as an administrator, broadcaster and journalist. “Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster, and journalist – truly one of our finest. His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms, and popular culture remains indisputable,” he said. Reflecting on the actor’s legacy, the President said Edochie had lived a fulfilled life and would continue to be remembered through his body of work. “Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully. “In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather,” Tinubu added. The President extended his condolences to the Edochie family, friends, associates and the Nigerian film industry on behalf of his family and the Federal Government. He concluded his tribute with a prayer for the late actor, saying, “May God Almighty grant ‘Ebube Dike’ eternal rest.” The post ‘Ebube Dike’: Tinubu pays tribute to late Nollywood legend Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tashima vows to serve single term if he wins FIFA election
item.description: FIFA presidential candidate Kozo Tashima said Wednesday that he planned to serve only one term of four years if he beats Gianni Infantino and Philippe Diallo in March’s election. Japan’s Tashima has pledged to restore “integrity” to world football’s governing body and is one of three names on the ballot along with current president Infantino and French football chief Diallo. Infantino has faced stinging criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup but he retains considerable support for his bid for a fourth and final term. Tashima admits that he has only an outside chance of winning but pledged to make his time in charge brief if he is elected. “I am currently putting together a manifesto but basically I plan to serve for one term of four years,” the 69-year-old told reporters in Tokyo. “In those four years I plan to focus on changing governance at FIFA. I believe we have to make the processes within FIFA more transparent.” Tashima said last week that he was not “at this point” thinking of dropping out of the race in order to give Diallo a straight fight against Infantino. Diallo has Europe’s backing and is seen as the likelier candidate to unseat the current president. Tashima said he had spoken to Diallo by phone and intends to meet him in person in Europe. He said they were both “heading in the same direction” and would consult over tactics. “As we go forward, if we continue to communicate we may find our direction does indeed align or we may find we have some differences,” he said. “The main goal is to bring FIFA back onto the right track, and we are looking at various options to achieve that.” The post Tashima vows to serve single term if he wins FIFA election appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Malaysia Sues Google For $146m Over YouTube Content
item.description: Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant’s failure to remove “harmful” content posted on video-sharing platform YouTube. “The lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google’s alleged failure to comply with its statutory obligations and applicable licence conditions,” the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said. The first suit related to the US firm’s alleged failure to take action against “thousands of online materials including gambling, scams and fraud”, the watchdog said in a statement. The MCMC said it had submitted 73,703 reports to YouTube between January 1 and October 28 this year, the majority of which related to online gambling. In this file photo taken on June 28, 2013 a webcam is positioned in front of YouTube’s logo in Paris. (Photo by LIONEL BONAVENTURE / AFP) Of these gambling-related reports, some 4,950 cases received no response, while a further 35 cases took more than 90 days for a platform response or takedown, the MCMC added. A further 1,468 cases exceeded 30 days from the date of submission, it added. “These figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content,” the watchdog said. The second case related to YouTube’s failure to take down alleged defamatory and false content posted by a Malaysian blogger after the MCMC received a complaint. Google could not immediately be reached for comment. The lawsuits came three weeks after Google announced plans to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure, expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024. The country is Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing hub for new data centres crammed with servers that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators. Malaysia had previously taken other major social media platforms, including TikTok, to task over allegations that they had failed to remove content deemed “grossly offensive”. item.title: Trump hails Infantino as USA to co-host 2031 Women’s World Cup
item.description: President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup. Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in July with a shortlived plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A FIFA election next March in Morocco will decide if Infantino keeps his job against rival contenders Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan. “Thank you to Gianni Infantino, and his great staff, for working to bring the Tournament to the USA,” Trump posted on social media. Trump and Infantino awarded Spain the trophy at this year’s final of the World Cup, which was co-hosted by Canada and Mexico. FIFA confirmed Monday that the United States will co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after Infantino noted it was the “sole candidacy” for the tournament. “I am proud to announce that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will take place in the United States!” Trump posted. “After hosting the Most Successful World Cup in History, no Country is better positioned than the United States to be home to the largest Women’s Sporting Event in History.” The Women’s World Cup field will expand to a record 48 teams in 2031. “The FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will bring Generational Economic Impact to the United States, grow the sport of Soccer throughout our Country and the World, and showcase America’s Exceptionalism,” Trump posted. item.title: 2027: ‘No Political Ambition Is Worth The Life Of A Nigerian’, IGP Warns Politicians
item.description: The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Tuesday warned politicians against turning the 2027 general elections into a theatre of violence. Speaking at a high-level security meeting in Abuja with the Independent National Electoral Commission, political party leaders, civil society organisations and other stakeholders, Disu described the growing incidents of political violence as a serious threat to public peace and democratic participation. He warned politicians to desist from violence, which has led to growing cases of reported killings across the country. “We are meeting at a particularly critical moment in our nation’s democratic journey. Recent incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and convoys, the use of dangerous weapons, intimidation of political opponents and the disruption of lawful political gatherings have become matters of serious concern. “These developments threaten public peace, endanger innocent lives and undermine confidence in our democratic institutions. They are warning signs that must be addressed decisively before they escalate into a broader threat to national security. “ Let me state categorically that political competition must never become a justification for violence. Democracy provides an opportunity for citizens to freely express their political preferences, support candidates of their choice and hold differing opinions without fear or intimidation. “It must never become a contest of who can mobilise more thugs, deploy more weapons or inflict greater harm on political opponents. No political ambition is worth the life of a Nigerian, and no electoral victory is worth the destruction of our national peace.” The IGP noted that the Force would not tolerate political violence, warning to take legal actions on those found guilty of employing thugs to intimidate and assault the public. “The position of the Nigeria Police Force is clear: we have zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the political party, candidate, personality or interest involved. Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable. “We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not to any political party or individual. We will protect the rights of all lawful political actors to organise rallies, hold meetings and participate in the democratic process. “However, we will not hesitate to take lawful and decisive action against anyone who engages in thuggery, intimidation, assault, the use of offensive weapons or any conduct capable of disrupting public peace. “I wish to remind all political actors that the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the INEC Regulations and other applicable laws prescribe clear standards of conduct and consequences for electoral offences. “Political office, party affiliation or personal influence does not place anyone above the law. item.title: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. item.title: My dad died from fake drugs — IMAN president
item.description: ……IMAN to introduce TIN for importers in 2027 By Efe Onodjae & Jacintha Ezugwu The President of the Importers Association of Nigeria (IMAN), George Ndubuisi, has said his personal experience of losing his father to fake drugs has strengthened his resolve to fight the importation and distribution of counterfeit and adulterated products in Nigeria. Ndubuisi, who disclosed that his father died in 2013 after taking drugs he described as fake, said the association would introduce an importer identification number in February 2027 to ensure that every imported container and its contents could be traced to a particular individual. He said this during an end of the year party with the association at the Apapa office, Lagos. According to him the initiative was designed to hold importers accountable for prohibited and substandard goods entering the country, while protecting clearing agents from bearing the consequences of import violations committed by their clients. The IMAN president said the proposed system would ensure that every container brought into the country was linked to a specific importer through shipping documents and other relevant records. He said, “In February 2027, IMAN is going to take a new position because the goalpost determines where you will put the goal. “We are shifting the goalpost to ensure that every container or import that comes into the country is tagged to a particular person. That gives room for an IMAN identification number, through which every importer registered on our platform is a confirmed importer. “If you are not on our platform, you are not an importer.” Ndubuisi said the initiative became necessary because some importers allegedly bring prohibited goods, including arms and ammunition, into the country without proper identification. He lamented that when such consignments are intercepted by the Nigeria Customs Service, clearing agents often bear the consequences while the importers disappear. He said the proposed identification system would make it difficult for importers to evade responsibility, adding that their identities would be traceable through shipping documents. “Even in the case of a breach, when Customs holds the goods, the people who suffer are the agents, while the importers go into hiding. “With this measure, we want to bring the importer to book. Even if you try to hide, your identity on the shipping documents represents who you are,” he said. The IMAN president explained that the identification number would be linked to the bank account of the importer, making it easier to establish ownership of imported goods and trace individuals responsible for bringing substandard products into the country. He said the system would also help identify importers involved in the importation of fake and adulterated products, which he described as a major threat to public health and the economy. item.title: Pete Edochie: Fans mourn Nollywood legend, recall iconic roles
item.description: Social media users and fans of veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, have taken to social media to mourn his death, describing it as the “loss of an iconic figure in Nigeria’s film industry”. His death was announced by his family in a statement shared on Instagram by his eldest son, Leo Edochie, through his account, @Edochieleo, on Wednesday. The statement said Edochie died in the early hours of Wednesday in Enugu after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. The actor’s death at 79 has attracted tributes, from fans with social media users recalling his memorable performances, distinctive voice and contribution to Nollywood. A fan, @UrchiL, described Edochie’s death as the loss of a legend, saying, “Things have really fallen apart, Nollywood has really lost a legend and an iroko. Rip Pete Edochie we would miss your legendary voice and proverbs in Nollywood movies.” Another fan, @chinedu, wrote, “An iroko has truly fallen. Rest easy legend.” @Adeyanju, described the actor as a giant whose death had deeply affected him, saying, “Indeed, Things Have Fallen Apart and the heavens have come to Collect!! This one pain me oh!!” @Brianjude wrote, “Rest in Peace Odogwu Chief Pete Edochie.” A user, @Rexemmy4, also lamented the actor’s death, saying, “Rest in peace Ebubedike. Sadly, 2026 has taken almost the whole Igwe council in Nollywood, and now it has even taken the Igwe too. Only the bodyguards remain now.” @Tobelani15 recalled the actor’s plans for his 80th birthday, saying he had mentioned the plans during an interview on Curiosity. @Tidal described Edochie’s life as fulfilled, saying his death should be celebrated while extending condolences to his family. item.title: Kwankwasiyya Supporters Carry Sticks But Harm Nobody, Obi Clarifies ‘Rig And Die’ Slogan
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified controversies surrounding the popular ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone. He spoke in an interview with Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State, after an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting. Addressing concerns over the presence of weapons at political gatherings, Obi said the public had misunderstood the ‘rig and die’ calls against electoral malpractice as opposition to political campaigns. This is as he defended supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, over allegations that they carry sticks to political campaigns, saying the items have not been used to “harm anyone”. Obi insisted that he had not witnessed anyone being attacked with the stick-wielding Kwankwasiyya movement during political gatherings. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” he said. Obi explained that the Kwankwasiyya movement, led by Kwankwaso, had a longstanding tradition of supporters appearing at political gatherings with sticks and similar items. He said, “Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody. “I’ve been part of that family for a while, and I’ve never seen one day, maybe behind me, that anybody was harmed because they were carrying such items.” The former Anambra State governor appealed to security agencies and other authorities to prevent violence during political activities, warning against the loss of lives over political ambitions. “So we’re pleading with the authorities. Please, we cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders,” he added. His comments came amid growing concerns over attacks on opposition political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. On Monday, gunmen attacked a campaign gathering of the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, leaving several people dead and others injured. Omo-Agege, a former Deputy President of the Senate, escaped the attack, while members of his campaign team and other supporters were among the casualties. item.title: Ronaldo deserves fitting farewell from Portugal, says Guardiola
item.description: Pep Guardiola has called on the Portuguese Football Federation to give Cristiano Ronaldo a fitting farewell from the national team, saying the forward deserves to end his international career with the recognition of his country. The former Manchester City manager made the appeal during an interview with former Brazilian footballer Romário on Tuesday, following Ronaldo’s announcement of his retirement from international football earlier this month. “Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn’t leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can’t let him go like this,” Guardiola said. “Both sides need to make an effort to guarantee a fitting farewell. He’s been an incredibly important figure, not only for himself and Portugal, but for future generations of Portuguese players.” He added that Ronaldo’s achievements deserved to be celebrated rather than overshadowed by a disagreement with members of the national team. “An entire career shouldn’t be judged based on a month or two, or because of a disagreement or misunderstanding with one or two individuals,” he said. “There are exceptional players, and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified.” Guardiola also called for a celebration in which Ronaldo would feel appreciated by Portuguese supporters, urging both parties to put their differences behind them. “There should be a celebration where he feels the love of his countrymen, and he, in turn, must also take the initiative and say: Let’s turn the page on the past,” he added. The disagreement between Ronaldo and Jesus came to public attention on September 30, when the forward left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen ahead of their Nations League fixture against Denmark. Ronaldo had been an unused substitute in Portugal’s 2-1 victory over Norway on September 27, despite warming up for about 30 minutes during the match. Jesus later admitted that Ronaldo was unhappy with his decision not to introduce him, while the forward subsequently accused the coach of breaking his word over an agreement concerning his playing time and the explanation of his omission. Ronaldo also apologised for his conduct following the incident but said he remained available for Portugal after serving any punishment imposed by the football authorities. However, on November 5, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a 23-year career with the national team. In his announcement, Ronaldo said it was time to hand back Portugal’s iconic No. 7 shirt, adding that the decision was not easy because it involved both his head and his heart. He finished his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, making him the most-capped player and highest goalscorer in men’s international football. Following his retirement, the Portuguese Football Federation redesigned the national team’s No. 7 shirt in tribute to the forward. item.title: Can We Prepare Children For Financial Success Before They Start Earning?
item.description: Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation. In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa. Why should financial education begin in childhood? Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children? Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions? A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly. Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early. Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day. The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions. The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely. We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master. item.title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations. Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.” In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry. “Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said. He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions. “He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said. Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart. The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema. Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs. His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji. In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours.
